message.content:
Sure! Those numbers point straight at **Google’s HQ – the “Googleplex”** in Mountain View, California.  
Below I’ll show what you’d get from a typical *reverse‑geocoding* request to the Google Maps Geocoding API, plus a quick guide on how to make the call yourself.

---

### What the API would return

If you hit:

```
https://maps.googleapis.com/maps/api/geocode/json?
    latlng=37.4224764,-122.0842499&key=[YOUR_API_KEY]
```

you should receive something like this (truncated):

```json
{
   "results" : [
      {
         "address_components": [
            {"long_name":"1600","short_name":"1600","types":["street_number"]},
            {"long_name":"Amphitheatre Pkwy","short_name":"Amphitheatre Pkwy","types":["route"]},
            {"long_name":"Mountain View","short_name":"Mountain View","types":["locality","political"]},
            {"long_name":"Santa Clara County","short_name":"SCl","types":["administrative_area_level_2","political"]},
            {"long_name":"California","short_name":"CA","types":["administrative_area_level_1","political"]},
            {"long_name":"United States","short_name":"US","types":["country","political"]},
            {"long_name":"94043","short_name":"94043","types":["postal_code"]}
         ],
         "formatted_address":"1600 Amphitheatre Parkway, Mountain View, CA 94043, USA",
         "geometry":{
            "location":{"lat":37.4224764,"lng":-122.0839285},
            "location_type":"ROOFTOP"
         },
         "place_id":"ChIJj61dQgK6j4ARw7eZ8YfXcEo",
         "plus_code":{"compound_code":"CWC8+R3 Mountain View, CA, United States","global_code":"849VCWC8+R3"},
         "types":["premise"]
      }
   ],
   "status":"OK"
}
```

> **Note:** The `location` field inside `geometry` will match your input exactly (`37.4224764`, `-122.0842499`). The rest gives you the human‑readable address and other metadata.

---

### How to run it yourself

| Step | Action |
|------|--------|
| 1️⃣ | Get a Google Cloud project & enable the **Geocoding API**. |
| 2️⃣ | Create an API key (restrict it as needed). |
| 3️⃣ | Build the URL shown above, replacing `[YOUR_API_KEY]`. |
| 4️⃣ | Send a GET request (curl, Postman, browser, JavaScript fetch, etc.). |

#### Example curl command

```bash
curl \
"https://maps.googleapis.com/maps/api/geocode/json?latlng=37.4224764,-122.0842499&key=AIzaSyD...yourKey..."
```

#### Quick Node.js / Fetch example

```js
const url =
  'https://maps.googleapis.com/maps/api/geocode/json?' +
  new URLSearchParams({
    latlng: '37.4224764,-122.0842499',
    key: 'YOUR_GOOGLE_MAPS_API_KEY'
  });

fetch(url)
  .then(r => r.json())
  .then(data => console.log(JSON.stringify(data, null, 2)))
  .catch(err => console.error('Error:', err));
```

---

### Bottom line

Those coordinates belong to **1600 Amphitheatre Parkway, Mountain View, CA 94043**, i.e., the Googleplex. If you plug them into the Geocoding API as shown, you'll see the same address returned along with all the usual place data.
